title: Choosing a managed provider: EKS, AKS and GKE

videos.script: Lesson 3 showed Kubernetes in two places: run by you, or run by a provider. This lesson is about the second. {{two}} A managed cluster still runs your pods on machines. What changes is who runs the part that decides. The API server, etcd, the scheduler, the upgrades. {{split}} Three providers sell most of these clusters. Amazon calls it EKS, Microsoft calls it AKS, and Google calls it GKE. {{three}} They agree on the Kubernetes part, because every one of them must pass the same conformance tests. They differ on everything around it: the fee, the support window, the network, and how much of the machines they take off your hands. {{differ}} You will read the fees from the providers' own price lists, and then draw the line of what is still yours. {{line}}
